topic: What antenna design considerations optimize ground station visibility during short service windows in LEO constellations?
consensus_response: To optimize ground station visibility, hybrid antenna designs combining phased arrays and shaped-beam antennas can adapt to changing satellite orbits. Integrating ephemeris data with Shadowed-Rician (SR) fading models enhances signal gain while minimizing interference during brief service windows. Machine learning-based antenna optimization further improves performance by adapting to changing satellite positions and velocities in real-time.
reference_context: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) constellations require a high level of system redundancy for coverage zones, with 60-70 satellites equally spaced in ascending nodes covering the whole surface of the earth. The time of satellite flight over a subscriber can range from 10 minutes to 20 minutes.
